findings.title: The offline BLOCK comes from a per-arm scripted model, not from removing the retry
findings.where: examples/langchain_quickstart/offline_model.py:48-53 (candidate flag); agent.py:27,29-30; arci.yaml:7-8 labels retry/no-retry; README.md:3-5; docs/recipes/langchain.md:22-25,64
findings.claim: The two offline arms differ in two ways, not one. The candidate drops the ToolRetryMiddleware retry, and its OfflineModel also gets candidate=True, which makes it answer "Done" on any error ToolMessage. The baseline's scripted model hits the `continue` branch, skips the error and reads the order again. So the baseline script recovers from tool errors at the model level even without the retry. Removing the retry alone produces no regression. The labels retry/no-retry and the agent.py comment "Candidate removes that retry: clean tests pass, injected exceptions expose it" attribute the BLOCK to the retry. Offline, a model-policy flag that only the candidate has actually causes it. The 'Using the same model isolates the retry change' framing holds only for real models.
findings.evidence: I ran counterfactual suites on copies in scratchpad/p3breview/honesty/, each one round with acknowledge_single_round. (v1) The candidate keeps max_retries=0 but uses OfflineModel(candidate=False): PASS, exit 0, minus=0 zero=96. (v2) The candidate keeps OfflineModel(candidate=True) but gets max_retries=1: PASS, exit 0, minus=0 zero=96. The shipped configuration gives BLOCK with minus=48. The regression therefore needs both the missing retry and the candidate-only abandon flag.
findings.fix: Choose one of two fixes. (a) Make the scripted policy identical for both arms: OfflineModel with no candidate flag, abandoning on an error for both arms. The retry middleware is then the only declared difference, and the baseline's middleware retry still hides the error. (b) Keep the current design but say plainly in the README, the yaml comment, the agent.py comment and the recipe that the offline candidate also has a different scripted error policy. Also say that removing the retry alone gives 96 ties offline.

findings.title: The failure table says setup ERROR happens only before the first model call, but the code applies it on every model turn
findings.where: src/arci/adapters/langchain.py:437-450 (model_started is reset on every wrap_model_call); docs/recipes/langchain.md:83
findings.claim: The recipe table says failures before the first model call are ERROR/harness_error. The code's rule is broader: any exception inside the inner model handler that comes before on_chat_model_start on the current model call becomes ERROR 'agent setup failed'. That includes later turns, after tools have already executed and changed state. So a failure caused by the agent's own conversation midway through a trial is scored as harness ERROR rather than FAIL, with a misleading 'setup' label.
findings.evidence: In the probe suite (scratchpad/p3breview/honesty/probe), probe p16-pre_start_late uses bind_tools that returns a RunnableLambda. It raises ValueError only once a ToolMessage is present. The trial recorded tool_finish lookup_order ok=True and then ended ERROR/harness_error with "LangChain adapter unsupported: agent setup failed: ValueError: message formatting failed on a tool message". The same ValueError raised inside _generate gives FAIL/crash (probe2, q00/q01).
findings.fix: Either track 'first model call started' once per trial rather than per call, so later pre-start failures become FAIL/crash, or change the table row and the adapter docstring to say 'before the provider call starts, on any model turn'.

findings.title: check.py grades any unrecognised action as a stock-note task
findings.where: examples/langchain_quickstart/check.py:15-22 (same file is scaffolded by arci init --langchain)
findings.claim: check() has no branch for an unknown `action`. Any value other than refund, refund_note or stock_note (a typo, or a new action a user adds to the scaffold) is silently graded against the stock-note expectations: refund 0 and note 'stock: N'. A correct end state then FAILs and a wrong one PASSes, and nothing errors. With the 24 shipped tasks, I found no wrong state that passes or right state that fails.
findings.evidence: Direct calls on the copy: action 'refund-note' with refunded_cents=total and notes ['refunded'] returned False. The same action with no refund and notes ['stock: 7'] returned True. action 'refund_full' with a correct full refund returned False. All three shipped actions graded correct states True.
findings.fix: Raise ValueError for an unknown action, so the trial becomes grader ERROR rather than silently misgrading. Optionally validate actions at load time.

findings.title: The README's run time is optimistic, and the test's 115 s subprocess timeout is close to the CPU cost
findings.where: examples/langchain_quickstart/README.md:33-35; tests/unit/examples/test_langchain_quickstart.py:46,67
findings.claim: The README promises about 50 seconds for the first offline run with four workers. The measured run took 60 s wall-clock. It used about 231 s of CPU (209 s user + 22 s system), because each trial pays roughly 1.2 s of LangChain import and setup. On a 2-core runner, --workers 4 needs about 115 s or more, which is the test's subprocess timeout.
findings.evidence: `time arci run arci.yaml --workers 4` on the copied example: 209.36s user 21.76s system 384% cpu 1:00.18 total, BLOCK exit 1, round 1.
findings.fix: State a range (for example 1 to 2 minutes, depending on cores). Size the test's timeout and worker count to the CI runner, or record the CPU cost.

reasoning:
I reproduced both counterfactuals on scratch copies in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ajay--claude-spares-spare-8K9guD/39ca2335-7a5a-47d9-a374-69d92a47e1d0/scratchpad/p3breview/skeptic-retry/{shipped,v1,v2}. I ran the full `arci run arci.yaml --workers 4` with tracing off and no Ollama. Shipped gives BLOCK, exit 1, round 1, minus=48 zero=48. v1 sets the candidate's model to `OfflineModel(candidate=False)` and keeps `max_retries=0`: PASS, exit 0, round 1, minus=0 zero=96. v2 keeps `candidate=True` and sets `max_retries=1` for both arms: PASS, exit 0, minus=0 zero=96. So the offline BLOCK needs both the missing retry and the candidate-only abandon branch at `offline_model.py:48-53`. With `candidate=False`, a tool error hits `continue`, `lookup_order` stays missing, and the script reads the order again. That is why removing the retry alone produces 96 ties.

The finding's documentation charge is overstated, which is why I narrowed it. README.md:3-5 already says "the candidate abandons the task". docs/recipes/langchain.md:24-25 says the fake candidate abandons the error and calls this "the intentionally planted behavioural difference". The README also calls the result a planted fixture. A first-time user is told the expected BLOCK and gets it, so this is not blocking. "Using the same model isolates the retry change" (README.md:81) is in the real-model section, where the `candidate` flag is not used, so that sentence is correct.

The real gap is narrower. Several places attribute the offline regression to the retry alone, and nothing says that the baseline's scripted model would recover from the error even without the middleware:
- the yaml labels retry/no-retry (arci.yaml:7-8 and src/arci/init.py:1002-1003);
- the agent.py comment "Candidate removes that retry: clean tests pass, injected exceptions expose it" (agent.py:30 and src/arci/init.py:804);
- the recipe line "Both scripts retry an empty read; only the baseline retries errors".

The scaffold in src/arci/init.py carries the same wording, so a fix there is needed too.
corrected_claim: The offline arms differ in two ways: the candidate loses the ToolRetryMiddleware retry, and its OfflineModel also gets candidate=True, which abandons the task on an error ToolMessage. The baseline's scripted model instead skips the error and reads the order again. I reproduced the shipped BLOCK (minus=48). Removing only the retry gives PASS with 96 ties, and so does applying only the abandon flag. README.md:3-5 and recipe lines 24-25 do disclose the candidate's abandon behaviour and call it the planted difference. Several places still attribute the BLOCK to the retry alone and never say that removing the retry alone yields no offline regression. These are the retry/no-retry labels and the agent.py comment ("Candidate removes that retry ... injected exceptions expose it"), in both the example and the init.py scaffold, plus the recipe phrasing. That is a wording and attribution problem, not a misleading verdict. Fix: say in the comment, labels and recipe that the offline candidate also has a different scripted error policy, and that removing the retry alone gives 96 ties offline. Or give both arms the same scripted policy.

findings.title: Replacing tasks as the README says gives PASS (exit 0) when every trial fails, because the offline model only understands the shipped order-desk wording
findings.where: examples/langchain_quickstart/README.md ('Replace the order desk, task facts and checker together'); agent.py settings() offline fallback; offline_model.py _generate; arci run verdict output
findings.claim: The README tells users to replace the tools, tasks and checker. It does not say that offline_model.py is hard-coded to the order desk: it parses ORD-\d+, needs the prompt to start with 'Refund' or 'Check', and uses fixed tool names. agent.py also falls back to it silently whenever the variables are unset. With new tasks, both arms fail every trial. The run reports 96 tied pairs and PASS, and the output does not separate both arms passing from both arms failing.
findings.evidence: Copy 'newdomain': the only change was ORD- to INV- in tasks.jsonl, then arci run with the variables unset. Result: 'VERDICT: PASS (exit 0) ... counts: minus=0, zero=96'. trials.jsonl shows baseline FAIL/crash 'ValueError: expected an order id' 96/96 and candidate the same 96/96. Copy 'changetask': rewording desk-01 to 'Please refund order ORD-101.' made both arms FAIL ('oracle rejected final state') in all 4 conditions. Using order id A-102 made both arms FAIL/crash with the same ValueError. Neither showed any warning on stdout or stderr.
findings.fix: In 'The files you edit', say that offline_model.py only solves the shipped tasks and must be rewritten or removed when the tasks change. In agent.py, do not fall back silently: for example, have the fake raise a setup or infrastructure-classified error (giving ERROR, not a tied FAIL) when the prompt does not match. Have run and gate print per-arm success counts (baseline x/N, candidate y/N) beside minus/zero/plus, so a 0% tie is visible.

findings.title: The model choice (env vars) and agent/tool code are not in the sealed registration, so different experiments get the same experiment id
findings.where: examples/langchain_quickstart/agent.py (ARCI_QUICKSTART_* read at trial time); README 'arci.yaml registers the tasks, agents, ...'; manifest.json
findings.claim: Which model each arm used is not recorded in the manifest or the trials. Neither are agent.py or tools.py edits. Fresh directories therefore produce the identical experiment id for materially different experiments, and a stored verdict cannot say what was compared. Prior-run accounting cannot tell a changed candidate from an unchanged rerun.
findings.evidence: Each in a fresh copy, all produced runs/langchain-order-desk@87c0183fd6...: the offline run (BLOCK), CANDIDATE=ollama:qwen3.5:4b-mlx-ctx32k (local stand-in langchain_ollama, PASS), both arms openai:gpt-4o-mini (ERROR), baseline middleware removed in agent.py (PASS), and an extra cancel_order tool in tools.py (BLOCK). grep for ollama|openai|qwen|ARCI_QUICKSTART in manifest.json and trials.jsonl: 0 matches. Manifest keys contain no model or code identity.
findings.fix: Make the resolved model ids part of the registration, for example as variant labels or agent arguments in arci.yaml, or have the run refuse/print the resolved per-arm model before trial 1. Change the README wording so it does not claim the agents are registered: only import references are. Say that switching models or editing agent.py does not change the experiment id.

findings.title: Setting only one model variable silently compares a real model with the scripted fake and can PASS
findings.where: examples/langchain_quickstart/agent.py settings(); README 'Switch to real models'
findings.claim: The README says to set both variables, but nothing enforces it. With only one set, one arm stays scripted. The run gives a confident verdict with no warning.
findings.evidence: Copy 'onevar' with only ARCI_QUICKSTART_CANDIDATE=ollama:qwen3.5:4b-mlx-ctx32k. A local langchain_ollama stand-in in the copy, not the server, played a model that re-reads after an error. Result: 'VERDICT: PASS (exit 0) ... counts: minus=0, zero=96', 59 s, no warning. The stand-in received temperature=0.0 and reasoning=False, which confirms the in-code settings.
findings.fix: In settings(), raise (a setup error, so ERROR) when exactly one of the two variables is set, or require both or neither. Keep the README sentence.

findings.title: The CLI cannot explain an ERROR or BLOCK: report/triage exit 3 'not built yet', and the docs do not say so
findings.where: README / docs/recipes/langchain.md (only bundle/replay are listed as unbuilt); arci report, arci triage; arci run stdout
findings.claim: After a verdict, the natural next step is to ask why. Both commands refuse with exit 3. The run output gives no cause. With a missing provider package, the user waits about a minute for 192 errored trials, and the actionable message exists only inside trials.jsonl.
findings.evidence: 'arci report runs/...' printed 'suite support for report is not built yet', exit 3. 'arci triage runs/...' printed 'suite support for triage is not built yet', exit 3. Copy 'missingprov' (both arms openai:gpt-4o-mini, provider package not installed): 58 s, then 'VERDICT: ERROR (exit 3) reason: errored pairs exceed max_errored_pairs ... errored=96'. stderr held only the store path. The cause appears only in trials.jsonl failure_detail: 'LangChain adapter unsupported: agent setup failed: ImportError: Initializing ChatOpenAI requires the langchain-openai package...'. 'unsupported' is also misleading for a missing package.
findings.fix: Say in the README and recipe that suite report/triage are not available yet, and give a one-line way to list failing trials and failure_detail from trials.jsonl. Print the first harness_error detail, or a per-condition/arm outcome table, on stderr when a run ends in ERROR. Consider checking that the provider can be imported before trial 1.

findings.title: Re-running init --langchain says 'use --force', but --force is rejected with --langchain
findings.where: src/arci/init.py run_langchain_init -> _check_output (line 257); src/arci/cli.py --langchain combination check; tests/unit/init/test_init_langchain.py:41 pins the message

findings.title: The step 5 glob fails after any second run, including an interrupted first attempt, with a confusing argparse error
findings.where: README step 5 'arci gate runs/langchain-order-desk@*'; arci gate argument error
findings.claim: Ctrl-C leaves a partial store, which is then recorded as a prior run. Re-running step 4 then makes the literal step 5 command fail with 'unrecognized arguments' and exit 3, which reads like an ERROR verdict. The README's caveat covers 'multiple runs', but a user who pressed Ctrl-C does not think of having two runs.
findings.evidence: Copy 'interrupt3': SIGINT after 12 s printed a KeyboardInterrupt traceback and left a store with 48 trials and no decision.json (gating it gives ERROR 'trial set is not a whole number of rounds'). Re-running step 4 printed BLOCK and 'prior runs: ...@87c0183...'. Step 5 then printed 'error: CliError: unrecognized arguments: runs/langchain-order-desk@87c0183...', exit 3. The same happens after a plain second run in 'example'.
findings.fix: README: 'If you ran or interrupted step 4 more than once, pass the run store path printed on stderr.' Make gate say it takes exactly one RUN_DIR. Handle KeyboardInterrupt without a traceback.

findings.title: The step 2 install command is unpinned; the last built release has no [langchain] extra
findings.where: README step 2 'pip install 'agent-reliability-ci[langchain]''
findings.claim: If the index serves an older release, pip only warns about the missing extra, and step 3 fails with an argparse error instead of a clear version problem. The README hedges this, but the command does not prevent it.
findings.evidence: dist-v0.8.0/agent_reliability_ci-0.8.0-py3-none-any.whl METADATA: Version 0.8.0, no Provides-Extra, Requires-Dist only pydantic and pyyaml, no langchain files. The worktree is 1.0.0. PyPI was not checked (no network).

findings.title: An added fault on a tool some tasks never call is silently diluted into ties
findings.where: arci.yaml conditions; run output
findings.claim: When a user adds a condition, nothing reports how many trials the fault actually fired in. Tasks that never reach the faulted tool count as clean ties.
findings.evidence: Copy 'addcond' added refund_timeout (tool_timeout on issue_refund): BLOCK, 120 pairs, minus=64. The fault fired in 16 of 24 baseline trials. In the other 8 (stock-note tasks) it never fired, and those pairs were counted as PASS/PASS ties, with no message. The recipe mentions this, but the README and the output do not.
findings.fix: Print a per-condition 'fault fired in k/N trials' line, or note it in the README's arci.yaml row.

(c) I set ARCI_QUICKSTART_CANDIDATE=openai:gpt-4o-mini. langchain_openai is not installed, so every candidate trial errored and the verdict was ERROR, exit 3.
All three wrote runs/langchain-order-desk@87c0183fd65465a107459b5216914ce0eddd22d16de9547a8b51eaa6cdd2b66b. Their manifest.json files are byte-identical (sha256 d22c3530...).
The manifest has baseline={label: retry, agent: 'agent:baseline', candidate_id: ''} and the candidate equivalent, fixtures_sha256='' and prior_runs=[]. It contains no model or code identity: a grep of manifest.json for openai|gpt|ollama|qwen|ARCI_QUICKSTART|max_retries finds 0 matches in all three. trials.jsonl also has 0 matches in (a) and (b). In (c) the only matches are the incidental ImportError text in the candidate trials' failure_detail, not a recorded model identity.
This is how the code works. suite_rule_sha256 (src/arci/suite_schedule.py) hashes only the manifest content. The model id is read from os.environ inside agent.py at trial time, so it cannot reach the manifest. ArmSpec does have a user-supplied candidate_id ("stable identity of the code under test", documented in docs/DESCRIPTOR.md), but the quickstart's arci.yaml, README and recipe neither set nor mention it.
Re-running in the same directory with a different candidate model gave a new id (5e74b728...). That is only because _suite_prior_runs treats any earlier run with the same agent ref as the same candidate and appends it to prior_runs. A changed model and an unchanged rerun are therefore recorded the same way.
The README's "arci.yaml registers the tasks, agents, ..." overstates things: only the import references are registered. This does not break the offline first run, which gives the correct BLOCK, so it is major, not blocking.

As a result, in fresh directories the offline run (BLOCK), a run with a different candidate model (ERROR) and a run with agent.py's retry settings edited all produced the same experiment id, langchain-order-desk@87c0183f..., with byte-identical manifests. A stored verdict cannot say which models or code were compared. In the same directory, prior-run accounting records a changed model exactly like an unchanged rerun, because it matches on the agent ref. The README's claim that arci.yaml "registers the ... agents" holds only for the import references. Alternatively, print or refuse on the resolved models before trial 1.
